# Turborepo starters

This Turborepo starter is maintained by the Turborepo core team.

## Using this example

Run the following command:

```sh
npx create-turbo@latest
```

## What's inside?

This Turborepo includes the following packages/apps:

### Apps and Packages

- `docs`: a [Next.js](https://nextjs.org/) app
- `web`: another [Next.js](https://nextjs.org/) app
- `@repo/ui`: a stub React component library shared by both `web` and `docs` applications
- `@repo/eslint-config`: `eslint` configurations (includes `eslint-config-next` and `eslint-config-prettier`)
- `@repo/typescript-config`: `tsconfig.json`s used throughout the monorepo

Each package/app is 100% [TypeScript](https://www.typescriptlang.org/).

### Utilities

This Turborepo has some additional tools already setup for you:

- [TypeScript](https://www.typescriptlang.org/) for static type checking
- [ESLint](https://eslint.org/) for code linting
- [Prettier](https://prettier.io) for code formatting

### Build

To build all apps and packages, run the following command:

```
cd my-turborepo

# With [global `turbo`](https://turborepo.com/docs/getting-started/installation#global-installation) installed (recommended)
turbo build

# Without [global `turbo`](https://turborepo.com/docs/getting-started/installation#global-installation), use your package manager
npx turbo build
yarn dlx turbo build
pnpm exec turbo build
```

You can build a specific package by using a [filter](https://turborepo.com/docs/crafting-your-repository/running-tasks#using-filters):

```
# With [global `turbo`](https://turborepo.com/docs/getting-started/installation#global-installation) installed (recommended)
turbo build --filter=docs

# Without [global `turbo`](https://turborepo.com/docs/getting-started/installation#global-installation), use your package manager
npx turbo build --filter=docs
yarn exec turbo build --filter=docs
pnpm exec turbo build --filter=docs
```

### Develop

To develop all apps and packages, run the following command:

```
cd my-turborepo

# With [global `turbo`](https://turborepo.com/docs/getting-started/installation#global-installation) installed (recommended)
turbo dev

# Without [global `turbo`](https://turborepo.com/docs/getting-started/installation#global-installation), use your package manager
npx turbo dev
yarn exec turbo dev
pnpm exec turbo dev
```

You can develop a specific package by using a [filter](https://turborepo.com/docs/crafting-your-repository/running-tasks#using-filters):

```
# With [global `turbo`](https://turborepo.com/docs/getting-started/installation#global-installation) installed (recommended)
turbo dev --filter=web

# Without [global `turbo`](https://turborepo.com/docs/getting-started/installation#global-installation), use your package manager
npx turbo dev --filter=web
yarn exec turbo dev --filter=web
pnpm exec turbo dev --filter=web
```

### Remote Caching

> [!TIP]
> Vercel Remote Cache is free for all plans. Get started today at [vercel.com](https://vercel.com/signup?/signup?utm_source=remote-cache-sdk&utm_campaign=free_remote_cache).

Turborepo can use a technique known as [Remote Caching](https://turborepo.com/docs/core-concepts/remote-caching) to share cache artifacts across machines, enabling you to share build caches with your team and CI/CD pipelines.

By default, Turborepo will cache locally. To enable Remote Caching you will need an account with Vercel. If you don't have an account you can [create one](https://vercel.com/signup?utm_source=turborepo-examples), then enter the following commands:

```
cd my-turborepo

# With [global `turbo`](https://turborepo.com/docs/getting-started/installation#global-installation) installed (recommended)
turbo login

# Without [global `turbo`](https://turborepo.com/docs/getting-started/installation#global-installation), use your package manager
npx turbo login
yarn exec turbo login
pnpm exec turbo login
```

This will authenticate the Turborepo CLI with your [Vercel account](https://vercel.com/docs/concepts/personal-accounts/overview).

Next, you can link your Turborepo to your Remote Cache by running the following command from the root of your Turborepo:

```
# With [global `turbo`](https://turborepo.com/docs/getting-started/installation#global-installation) installed (recommended)
turbo link

# Without [global `turbo`](https://turborepo.com/docs/getting-started/installation#global-installation), use your package manager
npx turbo link
yarn exec turbo link
pnpm exec turbo link
```

## Useful Links

# Feature: React Frontend Code Quality Cleanup

## What We're Building

A systematic refactoring of the apps/web React frontend to eliminate code duplication, standardize patterns, and improve developer experience. This cleanup extracts common dialog patterns, form utilities, loading states, error handling, and ensures consistent query key management across all React Query hooks.

## User Story

As a developer working on the frontend
I want reusable components and utilities for common patterns
So that I can build new features faster with less boilerplate and maintain consistency across the codebase

## Technical Approach

Extract duplicated patterns into reusable hooks and components following the existing feature-based architecture. Create utility libraries for error handling and validation. Standardize React Query cache key management using factory patterns. All changes maintain backward compatibility and follow existing code conventions (TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui patterns).

## Files to Touch

### Existing Files

- `apps/web/src/client/pages/projects/components/DeleteProjectDialog.tsx` - Refactor to use new BaseDialog and useDialogForm
- `apps/web/src/client/pages/projects/git/components/CreateBranchDialog.tsx` - Refactor to use new patterns
- `apps/web/src/client/pages/projects/components/ProjectDialog.tsx` - Refactor to use LoadingButton
- `apps/web/src/client/pages/projects/git/components/CreatePullRequestDialog.tsx` - Refactor to use new patterns
- `apps/web/src/client/pages/auth/components/LoginForm.tsx` - Refactor to use AuthFormCard and LoadingButton
- `apps/web/src/client/pages/auth/components/SignupForm.tsx` - Refactor to use AuthFormCard and LoadingButton
- `apps/web/src/client/pages/projects/git/hooks/useGitOperations.ts` - Add query keys factory pattern
- `apps/web/src/client/providers/WebSocketProvider.tsx` - Fix React import pattern
- `apps/web/src/client/components/ai-elements/branch.tsx` - Fix React import pattern

### New Files

- `apps/web/src/client/hooks/useDialogForm.ts` - Generic dialog form state management hook
- `apps/web/src/client/components/BaseDialog.tsx` - Reusable dialog wrapper with reset functionality
- `apps/web/src/client/components/ui/loading-button.tsx` - Button with integrated loading state
- `apps/web/src/client/components/ui/error-alert.tsx` - Reusable error alert component
- `apps/web/src/client/lib/error-handlers.ts` - Error handling utilities for mutations
- `apps/web/src/client/pages/auth/components/AuthFormCard.tsx` - Shared auth form card wrapper
- `apps/web/src/client/hooks/useDialogForm.test.ts` - Tests for useDialogForm hook
- `apps/web/src/client/components/ui/loading-button.test.tsx` - Tests for LoadingButton component
- `apps/web/src/client/lib/error-handlers.test.ts` - Tests for error utilities

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Foundation (Utilities and Hooks)

Create core utilities and hooks that other components will depend on:
- useDialogForm hook for form state management
- Error handling utilities
- Import pattern fixes

### Phase 2: Core Components

Build reusable UI components using the foundation:
- BaseDialog wrapper component
- LoadingButton component
- ErrorAlert component
- AuthFormCard component

### Phase 3: Integration and Refactoring

Apply new patterns to existing components:
- Refactor 4 dialog components
- Refactor 2 auth form components
- Standardize git operations query keys
- Add comprehensive tests

## Step by Step Tasks

**IMPORTANT: Execute every step in order, top to bottom**

### 1: Fix Import Patterns

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
- [x] 1.1 Fix WebSocketProvider React imports
        - Change `import React, { ... }` to `import { ... }`
        - File: `apps/web/src/client/providers/WebSocketProvider.tsx`
        - Only import hooks directly, not React namespace
- [x] 1.2 Fix branch component React imports
        - Change `import React, { ... }` to `import { ... }`
        - File: `apps/web/src/client/components/ai-elements/branch.tsx`
        - Verify component still renders correctly

#### Completion Notes

- Updated WebSocketProvider to use direct hook imports from 'react' instead of React namespace
- Updated branch component to import Children and isValidElement directly
- Replaced all React.Children and React.isValidElement calls with direct imports
- Changed React.ReactNode to ReactNode type import

### 2: Create Core Utilities

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
- [x] 2.1 Create error handler utilities
        - File: `apps/web/src/client/lib/error-handlers.ts`
        - Export `extractErrorMessage(error: unknown, fallback?: string): string`
        - Export `handleMutationError(error: unknown, fallbackMessage: string): void` with toast integration
- [x] 2.2 Create error handler tests
        - File: `apps/web/src/client/lib/error-handlers.test.ts`
        - Test Error instances, string errors, unknown errors

## Comprehensive Codebase Overview

Based on my exploration of the monorepo, here is a detailed analysis of the project:

### 1. **PROJECT TYPE & PURPOSE**

This is a **Turborepo monorepo** that creates a comprehensive platform for **managing and visualizing AI agent workflows**. It's designed as a full-stack web application that allows users to:
- Create and manage projects
- Execute AI agent workflows (via Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and other AI CLI tools)
- Interact with projects through a chat interface with AI agents
- Manage file trees and edit code
- Execute terminal/shell commands
- Track git repository state and manage branches/PRs

The project bridges AI CLI tools (like Claude Code) with a web UI, enabling collaborative AI-assisted development workflows.

---

### 2. **MONOREPO STRUCTURE**

The project uses **Turbo** for monorepo orchestration with **pnpm** workspaces. It contains:

#### **Apps:**
- **`apps/web`** - Primary full-stack web application (React frontend + Fastify backend)

#### **Packages:**
- **`packages/agent-cli-sdk`** (v4.0.0) - TypeScript SDK for orchestrating AI-powered CLI tools (Claude, Codex, Cursor, Gemini)
- **`packages/agent-workflows`** (v0.1.18) - Workflow utilities for building traceable, stateful workflows
- **`packages/ui`** - Shared UI component library 
- **`packages/eslint-config`** - Shared ESLint configuration
- **`packages/typescript-config`** - Shared TypeScript configuration

---

### 3. **TECHNOLOGY STACK**

#### **Frontend (React 19 + Vite):**
- **UI Framework**: React 19 with TypeScript
- **Bundler**: Vite
- **Routing**: React Router v7
- **State Management**: 
  - Zustand for global client state
  - TanStack Query (React Query) for server state
- **UI Components**: shadcn/ui (Radix UI + Tailwind CSS)
- **Code Editor**: CodeMirror v6
- **Terminal**: xterm.js (with node-pty backend)
- **Data Flow Visualization**: XYFlow
- **Forms**: React Hook Form + Zod validation
- **Charts**: Recharts
- **Styling**: Tailwind CSS v4

#### **Backend (Fastify + Node.js):**
- **HTTP Server**: Fastify v5
- **WebSocket**: @fastify/websocket
- **Authentication**: JWT via @fastify/jwt
- **Database**: Prisma ORM with SQLite
- **Validation**: Zod schemas
- **Security**: bcrypt password hashing
- **Rate Limiting**: @fastify/rate-limit
- **Terminal Management**: node-pty
- **Git Integration**: simple-git
- **AI Integration**: @ai-sdk/anthropic and @ai-sdk/openai

#### **Build & Dev:**
- **Build Tool**: Turbo (monorepo), tsx (TypeScript execution)
- **TypeScript**: v5.9.2
- **Testing**: Vitest
- **Code Quality**: ESLint 9, Prettier
- **Process Manager**: Designed for PM2/systemd in production

---

```
client/
├── pages/               # Feature-based pages

│       ├── components/ # Project dialogs
│       ├── hooks/      # useProjects hook
│       ├── files/      # File tree, editor, image viewer
│       ├── sessions/   # Chat with AI agents
│       ├── git/        # Git operations (status, commit, PR)
│       └── shell/      # Terminal emulator
├── components/         # Shared React components
│   ├── ui/            # shadcn/ui (Radix UI) components
│   └── ai-elements/   # Chat UI components
├── hooks/             # Shared custom hooks
├── stores/            # Zustand state stores
├── contexts/          # React contexts (AuthContext)
├── layouts/           # Layout components
└── lib/              # Utilities
```

**Backend (`server/`):**
```
server/
├── routes/           # API endpoints (auth, projects, files, git, shell)
├── services/         # Business logic (functional, not classes)
├── plugins/          # Fastify plugins (auth/JWT)
├── schemas/          # Zod validation schemas
├── websocket.ts      # WebSocket handler
├── agents/           # Agent-specific logic
└── utils/            # Helpers (error handling, path utils, etc.)
```

**Shared (`shared/`):**
```
shared/
├── types/           # Shared TypeScript types
├── utils/           # Shared utilities
└── prisma.ts        # Prisma client singleton
```

#### **Agent-CLI-SDK Package Structure:**
```
packages/agent-cli-sdk/src/
├── claude/         # Claude Code adapter
│   ├── index.ts    # ClaudeAdapter class
│   ├── types.ts    # Configuration types
│   ├── events.ts   # Event types & type guards
│   ├── cli-args.ts # CLI argument builder
│   └── parser.ts   # JSONL output parser
├── codex/          # OpenAI Codex adapter
├── cursor/         # Cursor IDE adapter (stub)
├── gemini/         # Google Gemini adapter (stub)
└── shared/         # Shared utilities
    ├── types.ts    # Base types (ExecutionResponse, StreamEvent)
    ├── errors.ts   # Error classes
    ├── spawn.ts    # Process spawning
    └── json-parser.ts # JSON utilities
```

Key Export: `getAdapter()` - Factory function to instantiate appropriate adapter

#### **Agent-Workflows Package Structure:**
```
packages/agent-workflows/src/
├── workflow/       # Core orchestration
│   └── Workflow.ts # Main workflow class
├── storage/        # Storage adapters
│   ├── BaseStorage.ts     # Abstract base
│   └── FileStorage.ts     # Filesystem persistence
├── types/          # TypeScript interfaces
├── utils/          # Helpers (logging, ID generation)
└── cli/           # CLI command utilities
```

Key Pattern: Workflow orchestration with pluggable storage adapters (Result pattern for error handling)

---

### 5. **KEY FEATURES & FUNCTIONALITY**

#### **Authentication & Authorization:**
- Single-user design (personal use)
- JWT token-based authentication
- bcrypt password hashing
- Protected routes with `preHandler: fastify.authenticate`

#### **Project Management:**
- Create, read, update, delete projects
- Assign projects to local filesystem paths
- Track project metadata (name, path, status)
- Prisma database models for persistence

#### **AI Agent Integration:**
- Support for multiple AI CLI tools (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini)
- Real-time streaming responses
- Session management for continuity
- Token usage tracking
- Structured JSON output extraction
- Image file handling for Claude vision

#### **Chat Interface (Sessions):**
- Real-time WebSocket communication
- Message streaming with visual feedback
- Session persistence
- Agent-specific metadata storage
- Message history tracking

#### **Slash Command System:**
- Custom command syntax (e.g., `/commit`, `/pr`)
- Commands stored in `.claude/commands/` directory
- Template expansion with variables
- Git integration commands

#### **File Management:**
- Directory tree browsing (recursive)
- Text file editing with CodeMirror (syntax highlighting)
- Auto-save (debounced 3s)
- Image preview
- Binary file handling
- Max 10MB file size support

#### **Git Integration:**
- Status checking (modified files, branch info)
- Commit creation (with optional AI-generated messages)
- Branch management (create, list, switch)
- Pull request creation (requires GitHub CLI)
- Simple-git based implementation

#### **Terminal/Shell:**
- Full xterm.js terminal emulator
- node-pty for PTY allocation
- WebSocket-based streaming
- Project context awareness
- Session cleanup on disconnect

#### **Database Models (Prisma):**
- `User` - Authentication & project ownership
- `Project` - Project metadata & configuration
- `AgentSession` - Chat session tracking
- `AgentMessage` - Message history
- Relations for proper data organization

---

### 6. **NOTABLE PATTERNS & ARCHITECTURE DECISIONS**

#### **Frontend Patterns:**
1. **Feature-Based Organization**: Code organized by feature (projects, sessions, files, git, shell) rather than by file type
2. **Zustand Stores**: Global state for UI and WebSocket data
3. **TanStack Query**: Server state management with query keys factories
4. **Custom Hooks**: Reusable hooks for features (useProjects, useFiles, useGitOperations, etc.)
5. **Path Aliases**: All imports use `@/client/`, `@/server/`, `@/shared/` aliases (no relative imports)
6. **React 19 Hooks**: Direct hook imports (not `React.useEffect`)

#### **Backend Patterns:**
1. **Functional Services**: Pure functions exporting business logic (no classes)
2. **Zod Validation**: Request/response validation with type inference
3. **Custom Error Classes**: NotFoundError, UnauthorizedError, ForbiddenError, ValidationError
4. **Graceful Shutdown**: Proper cleanup on SIGINT/SIGTERM
5. **Structured Logging**: Pino logger with context objects
6. **WebSocket Events**: Flat event naming with dot notation (e.g., `session.{id}.send_message`)

#### **Monorepo Patterns:**
1. **Workspace Dependencies**: Using `workspace:*` protocol
2. **Shared Configurations**: ESLint, TypeScript, type definitions
3. **Turbo Caching**: Build and task caching across workspace
4. **Type Safety**: Strict TypeScript throughout

#### **AI Integration Pattern (Adapter Pattern):**
- Pluggable adapters for different AI CLI tools
- Consistent interface: `execute(prompt, options) → Promise<ExecutionResponse>`
- Event streaming with JSONL parsing
- Session continuation via sessionId
- Error handling with domain-specific exceptions

#### **Workflow Orchestration Pattern (Result Pattern):**
- Methods return `Result<T, E>` for type-safe error handling
- No exceptions for expected failures
- State persistence to `.agent/workflows/logs/{id}/`
- Auto-incrementing step numbers
- Immutable state updates

---

### 7. **CURRENT DEVELOPMENT STATE**

**Active Branch**: `feat/final-react-refactor-v2`

**Recent Changes** (Modified files):
- React component cleanup and refactoring
- BaseDialog component improvements
- DiffViewer enhancements
- Data table UI updates
- Dialog components (DeleteProject, Project, CreatePullRequest)
- Git integration improvements (service refactoring, status tracking)
- Session components (ListItem, ToolCollapsibleWrapper)
- Tests for git service

**Ongoing Cleanup Spec**: React frontend code quality improvements
- Eliminating code duplication
- Standardizing dialog patterns
- Creating reusable form utilities
- Improving loading states

---

### 8. **KEY DIRECTORIES & THEIR PURPOSES**

| Directory | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| `apps/web` | Main web application |
| `apps/web/src/client` | React frontend |
| `apps/web/src/server` | Fastify backend API |
| `apps/web/src/shared` | Code shared between client & server |
| `apps/web/prisma` | Database schema & migrations |
| `packages/agent-cli-sdk` | AI CLI tool orchestration SDK |
| `packages/agent-workflows` | Workflow execution & persistence |
| `packages/ui` | Shared React component library |
| `.agent` | Agent-specific specifications & workflow logs |
| `.claude` | Claude Code custom commands |
| `scripts` | Build & utility scripts |

---

### 9. **PROJECT CONSTRAINTS & GUIDELINES**

From `CLAUDE.md` files:

**Frontend:**
- Don't use `.js`/`.ts` extensions in imports (handled automatically)
- Always use `@/` path aliases (never relative imports)
- Fix `useEffect` dependencies (no object references, only primitives)
- Zustand updates must be immutable (spread operations, new array/object references)
- Import React hooks directly: `import { useEffect, useState } from 'react'`

**Backend:**
- Services are pure functions (no classes)
- Use Zod schemas for all request/response validation
- Throw custom error classes for proper error handling
- Structured logging with context objects
- No `any` types (use `unknown` or proper types)

**Monorepo:**
- Use `pnpm` for package management (v10.19.0+)
- Node >= 18.0.0 required
- TypeScript 5.9.2 enforced
- Turbo for build orchestration

---

### 10. **DEPLOYMENT & PRODUCTION CONSIDERATIONS**

- **Single-User Design**: Currently designed for personal use (single login)
- **Database**: SQLite for simplicity (can be replaced with PostgreSQL for production)
- **CLI Tool Integration**: Requires actual CLI tools installed (Claude Code, etc.)
- **Process Management**: Supports PM2, systemd, Docker
- **Environment Variables**: JWT_SECRET, LOG_LEVEL, PORT, DATABASE_URL
- **Logging**: Pino with file rotation support
- **Build Output**: `dist/client/` (static assets) and server runtime

---

### **SUMMARY**

This is a sophisticated, production-ready full-stack application that serves as a **bridge between AI CLI tools and a modern web UI**. It enables developers to leverage powerful AI assistants (Claude, Codex) within a context-aware web interface, manage projects, execute commands, and maintain development workflows. The codebase demonstrates strong architectural patterns, comprehensive type safety, and modular design with clear separation of concerns. The monorepo structure allows independent evolution of the web app, CLI SDK, and workflow utilities while maintaining consistency through shared configurations.
